## ACCEPT — PR objectui#9894 is ready + auto-merge. ⭐ The card's own remedy framing was WRONG, and the dev measured past it.

Seat `domain:ui#2`, `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`. `check-governed-merges.mjs --test` on the FINAL 3-path list: **0 of 3**.

### ⭐ The card said 2 sites and 「renaming is mechanical」. There are **6**, and a blanket rename is a TRAP.

The first deliverable — re-measure the refusal at source, ⛔ not on the card's word — came back as the card said **and brought back three things the card never measured**:

| | measured on `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, resolved from `packages/app-shell` |
|:--|:--|
| ⛔ **no alias door** | `when` **and** `condition` together is still refused (`unrecognized_keys: ["condition"]`) ⇒ the remedy is a **rename**, ⛔ not an alias migration |
| ⭐⭐ **the inverse control, in the same run** | `ScriptValidationSchema` **ACCEPTS `condition` and REFUSES `when`** (`unrecognized_keys: ["when"]`) ⇒ **two spellings live at once** |
| **scope** | all six skeletons run through the spec: `script`, `cross_field`, `state_machine`, `format`, `json_schema` all parse — **only `conditional` was broken** |

⇒ ⭐ **a blanket rename to `when` would have broken the `script` and `cross_field` rules that were correct.** The key is resolved **per rule** through a `guardKey(type)` helper, because **one `conditionField` element serves all three** CEL-bearing types.

And the two sites the card never named are the ones that would have bitten: **`changeType`** reads `cur.condition` (the OLD type's key) and writes `next.condition` (the NEW type's). ⇒ changing only the skeleton — the card's 「mechanical」 framing — would have left the editor **unable to load the rule it had just written**.

### ⭐⭐ Why the 「never 422s」 promise went false with nothing going red — proved, ⛔ not argued

Nothing ever checked it, and each leg carries a firing control:

- `makeSkeleton` is **module-private** — named in exactly **1** file tree-wide, exported nowhere (control: 45 app-shell files name 「skeleton」);
- neither existing panel suite imports `@objectstack/spec` or calls any parser — **0** hits, with `vitest` hits in both files and `expect(` at 8 and 18 as the same-command control;
- the `conditional` type is exercised by **zero** existing panel assertions (control: the other five types appear 9 times across the same two files);
- the assertions that do cover skeletons use `toMatchObject` against **the panel's own idea of the key**.

⇒ ⭐ **a producer checked against itself stays green however it spells things.**

⚠️ And the proof is ⛔ not the reasoning above — it is the ablations: **under all three, the pre-existing suite stayed green, 9 passed every time**, including the one that restores the original defect verbatim.

### ⭐ The reportable green, and what the dev did with it

| ablation | new pin | pre-existing suite |
|:--|:--|:--|
| conditional skeleton back to `condition` | **RED** 3 failed | green 9 |
| `guardKey` always `condition` (the pre-fix editor) | **RED** 3 failed | green 9 |
| ⭐ `guardKey` always `when` (**the blanket rename**) | RED but **only 1 failed** | green 9 |

⇒ the careless 「fix」 this card invites cost **one** assertion, because only the conditional half of the shared editor was pinned. ⭐ **The dev added a symmetric script-side round-trip pin and re-ran: that ablation now fails 2.** ⛔ It did not report the green and move on — it strengthened the instrument the green exposed.

### The pin, and the sweep

`ObjectValidationsPanel.whenKey.test.tsx`, 12 tests. ⛔ **No source-text assertion** — that is precisely how the defect survived. It drives the real panel and runs what `onPatch` emits through the **spec's own** `ValidationRuleSchema` and `ObjectSchema`, for **every** rule type the New menu offers, both spellings, plus the type switch across them.

⭐ Sweep by the STRINGS, ⛔ not the path: every other consumer in the tree already spells it `when` for `conditional` — the types package docblocks, `ValidationPreview`, the objectui#9497 draft lint, the core engine, and the `packages/types` parity pin. ⇒ **this panel was the last producer disagreeing with its own tree.**

### ⭐ It cut two false sentences from its OWN changeset before pushing

(a) 「false from the start」 — ⛔ not derivable here, because this checkout is **shallow** (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` = true), so the oldest commit touching the skeleton is **the window edge, not an introduction**; (b) an enumeration of authoring routes carried over from a neighbouring changeset and never verified to reach **this** panel. Both replaced with what was measured, and the docblock quote verified verbatim with a typo-control at 0.

⇒ ⭐ that is 说明 ⑳ caught **on the write side, by the author**, which is where it is cheapest.

### ⚠️ One reading of the dev's that this seat does ⛔ NOT accept

> the only sibling worktree was … on branch `claude/issue-9859-repeater-grid-widget-detectors` — note the branch name is about repeater/grid widget detectors, **not** `SchemaForm.tsx` as the dispatch stated, so that line was stale.

⛔ **The dispatch was right and this inference is wrong.** objectui#9859's landed PR objectui#9887 modifies exactly `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx` — read from the PR's file list. ⇒ the dev inferred a **file surface from a branch name**, which is 说明 ⑮ in a new spelling: 「adjacency is measured from the other seat's **PR file list**, ⛔ not from its title」 — and ⛔ not from its branch name either.

⭐ It reached the right **action** anyway (different file, no serialization owed) and flagged the discrepancy instead of silently relying on it, which is why this is recorded as a reading to correct and ⛔ not a fault in the delivery.

### ⛔ Filed upstream, ⛔ not fixed here: **objectstack#19044**

The dev found `os-verify-lock.sh` returns **exit 126** on the direct invocation its own header documents, and worked around it with `bash <path>`. ⭐ The seat re-measured and the finding is **wider**: `git ls-files -s` reports **`100644`** for `os-verify-lock.sh` **and both its `.sh` siblings** in `scripts/pm/` ⇒ ⛔ not a lost bit on this container, the **tracked mode**.

⚠️ Why it matters beyond ergonomics: that script's own header teaches that **exit 99** means the lock was never acquired and that a caller must read the VERDICT line, never a bare `$?`. **126 is a number the header does not explain, from a call that never ran the command and printed no VERDICT line** ⇒ a dev reading `$?` records a **red gate that never ran** — the third instance of that shape measured today.

### ⚠️ The pending changeset — read, and deliberately ⛔ NOT edited

`.changeset/8167-conditionbuilder-mount-scope.md` declares `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` ⇒ it **publishes**. Its sentence 「An object validation rule's `condition` (`ObjectValidationsPanel`) declares `scope="record"`」 is **narrowed, ⛔ not falsified**: the mount still declares that scope for all three CEL-bearing types; the backticked `condition` now names two of them rather than three. ⇒ ⛔ **no edit.** A fence amendment is for a sentence the diff makes **false**, ⛔ not for one it makes **less complete** — and `8167` is another card's release declaration.

⭐ And `check:changeset-claims` printed 「No pending changeset names a file this change touches」 — **correct by its own rule**, which matches by backticked **file** name while `8167` names the panel by **symbol**. ⇒ the gap this seat's dispatch warned about, measured live. The manual sweep was the instrument; ⛔ the gate was not.

### Closing keyword and the card's end state

`Part of #9802`, verified: `Fixes` / `Closes` / `Resolves` all **absent**, `Part of` **present**. ⭐ The dev declined to close by keyword because the card left one remedy-shape question open — whether the panel should **surface the spec's suggestion text** rather than silently writing the corrected key — and a closing keyword would decide that at merge.

⇒ **This seat closes the card by hand once the PR lands, and states the reason rather than letting it lapse:** this panel is a **no-code editor**. An author picks a rule type from the New menu and never types a key name, so the spec's 「Did you mean `condition` → `when`?」 has ⛔ no author-facing role **here**. If that suggestion is wanted on a surface where authors do type keys — the JSON source editor — that is a different surface and its own card, ⛔ not a remainder of this one.
